newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SWITZERLAND'S UBP RATES RICHTER AS "BUY".
newsitem.headline: SWITZERLAND'S UBP RATES RICHTER AS "BUY".

text.p: A Swiss bank report on Hungarian company Richter Gedeon Rt described the pharmaceutical firm as an outstanding play in eastern Europe, rating the shares as "buy".

"Gedeon Richter offers an exposure to the dynamics of the emerging markets of eastern Europe, enhanced by the strong growth of healthcare spending expected in this region," Geneva-based private bank Union Bancaire Privee (UBP) said in a company update.

Analyst Sabine Roggen listed a number of reasons to back her enthusiasm over Richter in the report, although she told Reuters that in the short-term fears over Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health could affect investor confidence in the company.
"The reduced political visibility in case Yeltsin dies could put pressure on the stock," she said.
Richter has a competitive edge over other western producers thanks to low-cost and soft currency-based production, the analyst said, adding that hard currency earnings meant an additional plus.
She added that Richter has the largest sales and distribution network of any Hungarian drugs firm the Eastern Europe, especially in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
"(This) represents the best choice for foreign companies eager to establish a footing in the region," she said, adding that the CIS represents Richter's most important single export market.
"Although the current economic and political situation remains difficult, the margins achieved and the huge potential make Richter's unique position very promising."
Healthcare spending per person in the CIS is curently estimated at 25 times lower than in Hungary.

Roggen said a further positive factor was that Richter, which has a broad range of products with no product accounting for more than 20 percent of sales, is boosting its profits steadily as a result of cost-cutting efforts and the concentration of higher-margin products.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Richter closed at 8,500 forints, down 100, on Monday.
